Article 17
(1) The integration of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons shall be incorporated into planning and budget documents which include the Regional Long-Term Development Plan (RPJPD), Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD), Strategic Plan of Regional Work Units (Renstra SKPD), Regional Government Work Plan (RKPD), and Work Plan and Budget of Regional Work Units (RKA-SKPD) and related SKPD RKA.
(2) The preparation of planning and budget documents as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be harmonized among related Regional Work Units (SKPD).
(3) The SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection together with P2TP2A shall facilitate the integration of policies, programs, and activities for empowerment, protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons into the preparation of planning and budget documents as set forth in paragraph (1).
(4) In implementing as referred to in paragraph (3), the SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection together with P2TP2A shall coordinate with the Regional Development Planning Agency.

Article 25
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women for the following year.
(3) The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 9
(1) The system for implementing protection for victims of human trafficking and violence against women and children is carried out through 2 (two) methods, namely:
a. Preventive method or prevention; and
b. Repressive method or handling (2) The preventive method or prevention is carried out through various forms of protection, both by the community and the government, which is intended to prevent the occurrence of criminal acts of human trafficking and violence or victims of violence against women and children.
(3) The repressive method or handling is carried out through various forms of protection conducted by the government through regulatory activities, implementation and enforcement of laws and regulations governing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking.
(4) The Guidelines and Technical Procedures for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking shall be further regulated through a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER XII
CRIMINAL PROVISIONS
Article 29
Every person who commits a criminal act of violence that is physical, psychological, sexual in nature, neglect, human trafficking, exploitation or that falls under the category of human trafficking, as well as other violence shall be threatened with criminal punishment as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VII
IMPLEMENTATION
Article 18
(1) The Regent implements policies, programs, and activities to eliminate all forms of discrimination and acts of violence against women and child victims of violence and human trafficking.
(2) The implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be coordinated by the Vice Regent.
(3) The Office of Women's Empowerment and Family Planning or SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection together with P2TP2A shall implement the policies, programs and activities that have been established, and in their implementation shall cooperate with related SKPDs, law enforcement agencies, community institutions, universities, and civil society.
(4) The implementation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be in the form of: policy analysis, coordination, advocacy, socialization, communication, information and education (KIE), training, service facilitation, service provision, development of women and child protection models and other forms.

Article 20
(1) In implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and human trafficking, the district government may cooperate with international institutions.
(2) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including trafficking in persons has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to education level, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, as well as particular ethnic groups, ethnicities, or races. One of the causes among them is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.
That violence and trafficking in persons that has been occurring is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.
According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and Jaringan Penanggulangan Anak Indonesia (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore there needs to be firm law enforcement, because in addition to the state, Regional Governments also have the obligation and responsibility to prevent and impose sanctions on acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, recovery and compensation to victims of violations.
Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Raperda can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal foundation for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons as well as guarantee the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

1.1.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the regulation is broadly about “kekerasan terhadap perempuan dan anak” and “perdagangan orang.” It defines violence types (fisik/psikis/seksual) and mentions “penelantaran” in Pasal 29, and it references the national Domestic Violence Law (UU 23/2004 PKDRT) only in the legal basis (“Mengingat” point 14). However, the operative provisions do not explicitly frame violence as “kekerasan dalam rumah tangga” (domestic/household violence) or specify violence occurring within the household/family as a distinct scope category. The judge’s ‘No’ rationale (no explicit domestic/household context in the provided text) aligns with the Indonesian content; therefore the golden ‘Yes’ likely over-credited the mere citation of UU PKDRT or inferred domestic violence without explicit coverage.

1.5.evaluator_rationale: While the policy mentions restoring victims’ economic conditions and provides economic independence services, the candidate sentences do not explicitly identify economic violence/economic abuse or domestic neglect as a form of violence against women.

(2) Facilitation and provision of services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided for women and children victims of violence including victims of trafficking in persons, women and children in conflict-prone and disaster areas, women and child workers, elderly women, women and children with disabilities, women and children victims of sexual exploitation, women heads of households, and women and children of other vulnerable groups.

(1) The system for implementing protection for victims of human trafficking and violence against women and children is carried out through 2 (two) methods, namely:

b. TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi.
4. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency.
5. Woman is a person of female gender.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
8. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and/or fainting and/or cause of death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery.
15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial.
16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and obscenity.
17. Recruitment is an action that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community.
18. Transfer is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place.
19. Debt bondage is the act of placing a person in the status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people who are their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment.
20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination.
22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred.
23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathically and explore problems to provide counseling in efforts to strengthen the victim psychologically.
25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as KPPA, is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics.
26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process.
27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved.
29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance.
32. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter referred to as SPO, is a procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree.
33. Discrimination against women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women;
34. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms.
35. Community institution is an institution formed by members of the Indonesian citizen community voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations.
36. Companion institution is an institution that provides assistance to women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons in Banyuwangi Regency.
37. Empathy is a mental condition that makes a person feel themselves to be in the same state of feelings or thoughts as the person or group who is a victim of violence and trafficking in persons.

Article 25
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women for the following year.
(3) The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(3) The SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection together with P2TP2A shall facilitate the integration of policies, programs, and activities for empowerment, protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons into the preparation of planning and budget documents as set forth in paragraph (1).

1.5.rationale: The Indonesian text does not define or list “kekerasan ekonomi” (economic violence/abuse) as a form of violence. It does mention restoring victims’ “kondisi ... ekonomi” (Pasal 3 huruf d) and provides “pelayanan kemandirian ekonomi” (Pasal 12 huruf e) as a recovery/empowerment service, and restitution covers “kehilangan kekayaan atau penghasilan” (Pasal 5 huruf a). These are about economic recovery/compensation, not recognizing economic abuse as a violence type. Since the regulation’s violence typology is physical/psychological/sexual (Pasal 1 angka 11–13) plus trafficking/exploitation/neglect in Pasal 29, the judge’s ‘No’ is consistent with the Indonesian source; the golden ‘Yes’ appears to conflate economic recovery measures with economic violence.

I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including trafficking in persons has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to education level, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, as well as particular ethnic groups, ethnicities, or races. One of the causes among them is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.
That violence and trafficking in persons that has been occurring is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.
According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and Jaringan Penanggulangan Anak Indonesia (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore there needs to be firm law enforcement, because in addition to the state, Regional Governments also have the obligation and responsibility to prevent and impose sanctions on acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, recovery and compensation to victims of violations.
Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Raperda can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal foundation for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons as well as guarantee the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

CHAPTER VII
IMPLEMENTATION
Article 18
(1) The Regent implements policies, programs, and activities to eliminate all forms of discrimination and acts of violence against women and child victims of violence and human trafficking.
(2) The implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be coordinated by the Vice Regent.
(3) The Office of Women's Empowerment and Family Planning or SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection together with P2TP2A shall implement the policies, programs and activities that have been established, and in their implementation shall cooperate with related SKPDs, law enforcement agencies, community institutions, universities, and civil society.
(4) The implementation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be in the form of: policy analysis, coordination, advocacy, socialization, communication, information and education (KIE), training, service facilitation, service provision, development of women and child protection models and other forms.

Article 9
(1) The system for implementing protection for victims of human trafficking and violence against women and children is carried out through 2 (two) methods, namely:
a. Preventive method or prevention; and
b. Repressive method or handling (2) The preventive method or prevention is carried out through various forms of protection, both by the community and the government, which is intended to prevent the occurrence of criminal acts of human trafficking and violence or victims of violence against women and children.
(3) The repressive method or handling is carried out through various forms of protection conducted by the government through regulatory activities, implementation and enforcement of laws and regulations governing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking.
(4) The Guidelines and Technical Procedures for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking shall be further regulated through a Regent Regulation.

Article 17
(1) The integration of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons shall be incorporated into planning and budget documents which include the Regional Long-Term Development Plan (RPJPD), Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD), Strategic Plan of Regional Work Units (Renstra SKPD), Regional Government Work Plan (RKPD), and Work Plan and Budget of Regional Work Units (RKA-SKPD) and related SKPD RKA.
(2) The preparation of planning and budget documents as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be harmonized among related Regional Work Units (SKPD).
(3) The SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection together with P2TP2A shall facilitate the integration of policies, programs, and activities for empowerment, protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons into the preparation of planning and budget documents as set forth in paragraph (1).
(4) In implementing as referred to in paragraph (3), the SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection together with P2TP2A shall coordinate with the Regional Development Planning Agency.

Article 25
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women for the following year.
(3) The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi.
4. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency.
5. Woman is a person of female gender.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
8. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and/or fainting and/or cause of death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery.
15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial.
16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and obscenity.
17. Recruitment is an action that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community.
18. Transfer is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place.
19. Debt bondage is the act of placing a person in the status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people who are their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment.
20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination.
22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred.
23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathically and explore problems to provide counseling in efforts to strengthen the victim psychologically.
25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as KPPA, is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics.
26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process.
27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved.
29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance.
32. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter referred to as SPO, is a procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree.
33. Discrimination against women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women;
34. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms.
35. Community institution is an institution formed by members of the Indonesian citizen community voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations.
36. Companion institution is an institution that provides assistance to women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons in Banyuwangi Regency.
37. Empathy is a mental condition that makes a person feel themselves to be in the same state of feelings or thoughts as the person or group who is a victim of violence and trafficking in persons.

Article 19
(1) The implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and human trafficking shall be carried out by establishing, developing, strengthening, or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions.
(2) The membership of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of relevant SKPD, law enforcement, community institutions, universities, and civil society.
(3) The establishment of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be determined by Regent's Decree.

4.4.rationale: The Indonesian regulation contains prevention framing and explicitly names education-type measures. Pasal 7 huruf a obligates the local government to conduct prevention efforts (“pencegahan terjadinya tindak pidana... dan kekerasan”), and Pasal 18 ayat (4) includes “informasi dan edukasi (KIE)” and “sosialisasi” as implementation activities. This supports that prevention is pursued through education/awareness activities. Thus the judge’s ‘Yes’ matches the Indonesian text; the golden ‘No’ appears wrong or based on a narrower definition of ‘education’ than what the regulation states.

7.3.translated_snippet: (1) In implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and human trafficking, the district government may cooperate with international institutions.
7.3.evaluator_rationale: The policy states that the district government may cooperate with international institutions in implementing protection policies and activities, which constitutes explicit international support/engagement (even if not framed as direct donor funding).

7.3.rationale: The Indonesian funding clause (Pasal 27) states funding comes from APBD Kabupaten Banyuwangi and “penerimaan lain-lain yang sah dan tidak mengikat” (other legitimate, non-binding revenues). It does not mention international donors or foreign funding sources. Pasal 20 only says the district government “dapat melakukan kerjasama dengan lembaga internasional” (may cooperate with international institutions) in implementing programs, which is cooperation/partnership, not donor funding. The retrieved English passages contained both Pasal 27 and Pasal 20, so the judge had enough information to distinguish cooperation from donor funding but still labeled ‘Yes’ by equating cooperation with international donors. That is a reasoning error given the indicator is specifically about funding sources/international donors.
